summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis, opioid use disorder, and diastolic heart failure was admitted after being found altered at home following alcohol relapse. He presented with alcohol withdrawal symptoms, abdominal pain, and leg edema. He was managed in the MICU with a phenobarbital taper, thiamine, and multivitamins. Electrolyte abnormalities including hypokalemia and hypophosphatemia were corrected with aggressive repletion. Diuretics were restarted for volume overload due to diastolic heart failure. Iron deficiency anemia was identified and treated with oral iron. He was stabilized, transitioned to oral medications, and discharged home with follow-up plans for his liver, heart, and substance use. He was strongly advised to abstain from alcohol.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver without ascites
